{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.6,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R78"],
      "pins": ["R78.1", "R78.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R78 is valued \"24k\" (SPICE: \"R78 VOUTN VOUTP 24k\"), but its own library description and MPN describe a 24 Ω part (\"...±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor\", MPN FRC0805J240TSD).",
      "expected": "A 24 Ω resistor across VOUTN–VOUTP, matching the part's description and MPN. A 24 kΩ value would be a different, much higher-impedance element.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R78\") (value \"24k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "100mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R78 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "The resistance across the bipolar output pair is 1000x off the part's rating. This changes the loading and balance of the VOUTP/VOUTN supply, and it may not match the intended resistor.",
      "confidence": 0.6
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D6", "D19", "D23"],
      "pins": ["D6.2", "D19.2", "D23.2"],
      "nets": ["/NET0145"],
      "observed": "The anodes of D6, D19 and D23 all sit on /NET0145, and that net has no other connection. It is not tied to +3V3 or any other supply, so the three LEDs have no forward-bias source. Their cathodes are driven only through R48, R74 and R84 from the active-low PI_nLED_Activity, Ethernet_nLED2 and Ethernet_nLED3 pins.",
      "expected": "Status LEDs with active-low drive need their anode tied to the 3.3 V rail, as the other status LEDs in the design are (for example D30 via R1 to +3V3).",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"30\") (name \"/NET0145\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D19\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D6\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D23\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "The three status LEDs (activity and Ethernet link/speed indicators) cannot light, so the board's status indication is lost.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    },
    {
      "category": "short_to_supply",
      "components": ["U4"],
      "pins": ["U4.2", "U4.5"],
      "nets": ["+5V"],
      "observed": "The data input A (pin 2) of buffer U4 is on the +5V net, so its output Y drives D25 high permanently. Its /OE pin is held by R24 to +3V3.",
      "expected": "A buffer used as a signal driver should have its A input driven by a logic signal. Other buffers in the design take their inputs from GPIO, CAN or control nets.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U4\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"2\") (name \"+5V\") (class \"High Power\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "If this is not intended as a fixed 5 V indicator, the circuit is stuck on and cannot be controlled.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The clearest deviation is R78, whose value of 24k contradicts its own 24 Ω description and MPN. A floating LED anode net (/NET0145) and a buffer input tied to +5V are lower-confidence candidates."
}

anomalies.observed: R78 is valued "24k" (SPICE: "R78 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"), but its own library description and MPN describe a 24 Ω part ("...±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor", MPN FRC0805J240TSD).
anomalies.expected: A 24 Ω resistor across VOUTN–VOUTP, matching the part's description and MPN. A 24 kΩ value would be a different, much higher-impedance element.
anomalies.impact: The resistance across the bipolar output pair is 1000x off the part's rating. This changes the loading and balance of the VOUTP/VOUTN supply, and it may not match the intended resistor.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of D6, D19 and D23 all sit on /NET0145, and that net has no other connection. It is not tied to +3V3 or any other supply, so the three LEDs have no forward-bias source. Their cathodes are driven only through R48, R74 and R84 from the active-low PI_nLED_Activity, Ethernet_nLED2 and Ethernet_nLED3 pins.
anomalies.expected: Status LEDs with active-low drive need their anode tied to the 3.3 V rail, as the other status LEDs in the design are (for example D30 via R1 to +3V3).
anomalies.impact: The three status LEDs (activity and Ethernet link/speed indicators) cannot light, so the board's status indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: The data input A (pin 2) of buffer U4 is on the +5V net, so its output Y drives D25 high permanently. Its /OE pin is held by R24 to +3V3.
anomalies.expected: A buffer used as a signal driver should have its A input driven by a logic signal. Other buffers in the design take their inputs from GPIO, CAN or control nets.
anomalies.impact: If this is not intended as a fixed 5 V indicator, the circuit is stuck on and cannot be controlled.
